Improve a model step by step, from score tests and predictive checks

Source: R/ctModelImprove.R
ctModelImprove.Rd

Starting from a fitted model, repeatedly screens it with ctScoreTest, refits it with the most strongly indicated relaxations one at a time, starting from the current estimates, and keeps the best of them if the refit's likelihood confirms it. The search stops when no relaxation is indicated and ctFitAdequacy finds the model adequate. When nothing is indicated but the model is not adequate, it tries structural changes in the same way: a slow process driving a latent (ctModelSlowComponent), a cycle such as a daily rhythm (ctModelPeriodicComponent), a process of its own for an item (ctModelUniqueProcess), a higher order latent process (ctModelHigherOrder), and any models given in candidates. These are ranked by the adequacy check's evidence for them: a slow process for a latent whose updates stay correlated over time gaps (the latent family), a cycle at the period the periodic family points to, and a process of its own for an item whose errors stay correlated over time (the residuals family).

Usage

ctModelImprove(
  fit,
  covariates = NULL,
  relax = c("heterogeneity", "covariates", "statedependence", "volatility", "fixed",
    "level", "slow", "unique", "periodic", "order"),
  changes = NULL,
  candidates = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  maxsteps = 10L,
  ntry = 3L,
  criterion = c("LR", "AIC", "BIC"),
  adequacy = TRUE,
  prune = TRUE,
  close = NULL,
  holdout = 0,
  form = "auto",
  periods = NULL,
  nsamples = 100L,
  projection = "auto",
  cores = getOption("mc.cores", 2L),
  checkpoint = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

fit

A fit from ctFit with backend = 'julia'.

covariates

Optional subject level covariates the model may add, as for ctScoreTest.

relax

Which relaxations may be made.

changes

Optional rows of ctModelProposals. The first round refits with these, in the order given, instead of screening, and keeps the first that improves the fit by criterion. With maxsteps = 1 this is one step of a search made by hand. Later rounds screen as usual.

candidates

Optional list of alternative models (from ctModel) to try when the screen finds nothing but the checks fail.

alpha

Level for the screen (Benjamini-Hochberg within each family), for the likelihood ratio decision, and for adequacy.

maxsteps

Maximum number of refit rounds.

ntry

Maximum number of proposals from the score tests refitted in a round, one at a time, the strongest first, keeping the first that improves the fit. Proposals from the adequacy check are tried in the same way until one improves the fit or none is left. Pruning and held-out confirmation refit this many at a time.

criterion

'LR', 'AIC' or 'BIC'.

adequacy

Use ctFitAdequacy to decide when to stop.

prune

After the search, try dropping each kept change in turn, and drop it if the likelihood does not need it given the others. A change kept early can be made unnecessary by one kept later.

close

Optional root mean square residual correlation regarded as a close enough fit to stop at (see Selection and confirmation).

holdout

Share of subjects, between 0 and 0.5, held out of the search to confirm its changes on.

form

How covariates are screened, as for ctScoreTest. 'threshold' lets the search add a covariate as a step.

periods

Periods for the adequacy check's periodic family, as for ctFitAdequacy. By default a range is scanned.

nsamples

Number of generated datasets for the adequacy checks.

projection

How the adequacy checks account for estimation, as for ctFitAdequacy.

cores

Cores for fitting and testing. With two or more cores, once a refit has taken longer than five minutes, the refits for pruning and for held-out confirmation run in parallel worker processes, ntry at a time, each with an equal share of cores. options(ctsem.improve.processes = FALSE) keeps them in this session.

checkpoint

Optional file the search saves its state to after every round and after pruning. Called again with the same file, fit and settings, the search resumes after the last round saved. A file from a different search is refused. With verbose, the refit in progress is also saved every ten minutes (<checkpoint>.refit.rds), with the round, the change, the iteration and the raw parameters reached.

verbose

Report progress: each round's steps, each refit's time, and while a refit runs, its iteration, objective and gradient every ten minutes.

Value

An object of class ctModelImprove, containing: fit, the final fit; history, every refit tried, with the round, the relaxation, its screening p-value, the change in log likelihood and parameters, the criterion's verdict and whether it was kept (a row with family 'prune' says whether the change was dropped, and a 'rank' row whether the lower rank was kept); screens, the score tests of each round; adequacy, the final checks; confirmation, with holdout, each kept change's likelihood ratio test on the held-out subjects; and stopped, why the search ended: 'adequate' (no adequacy family detected misfit), 'close fit' (those that did were shown to be within close), 'not adequate, no candidate improved' or 'not adequate, nothing left to try' (the checks still detect misfit), 'nothing indicated' (with adequacy = FALSE, the screen found nothing) or 'maxsteps'. A refit that failed, or ended below the model it extends, is in history with a note. With holdout, fit is the model with the confirmed changes refitted to every subject, and selected is the search's own choice fitted to the subjects it searched on.

Details

The relaxations, in terms of the model:

heterogeneity

indvarying = TRUE for a parameter and the T0MEANS parameters. For a fixed MANIFESTMEANS cell, a parameter that varies around the fixed value as its stated mean.

covariates

A covariate added as a time independent predictor, with effects on the parameters its tests pick out. For a predictor the model already has, effects on further parameters its tests pick out.

statedependence

A term d * eta_k * eta_m in a latent's drift, written into CINT with d a PARS parameter, so that a drift coefficient varies with a state.

volatility

A latent's innovation sd scaled by exp(v * eta_m), so that the size of the innovations depends on a state.

fixed

A cell fixed at zero is freed: a drift cross effect, a diffusion covariance or a cross loading.

level

A parameter of the dynamics or error variances that depends on a subject's level (a random intercept) is allowed to vary over subjects, correlated with the intercepts (see the level tests of ctScoreTest).

slow

A slow process driving a latent through its drift, with its effect starting at one and its persistence at a tenth of the latent's. If the model already has a slow process for another latent, letting that process drive this latent too is tried first.

periodic

A cycle of the period the adequacy check points to, driving every latent that has innovations. Each subject's phase is set from the clock at its first row and can deviate from it. The phase predictors are added to the data.

unique

A persistent process of its own, loading on one item. Where the pairs family finds two items' errors correlated within an occasion, a process shared by the two (ctModelUniqueProcess(shared = TRUE)) is tried too, treating such correlation as a process faster than the occasions. Like the other structural changes, this is tried only once the score tests indicate nothing.

errorcov

Not by default. A measurement error covariance the score test flags is freed, instead of proposing a shared process. This is for designs with a reason for correlated errors, such as a method the items share.

order

A latent process made second order.

On a reduced rank level (poprank), a heterogeneity result for a parameter that already varies through the shared dimensions gives it a variance of its own (popunique). Without reduced rank, a significant dimension test makes the parameters in its direction vary together. Relaxations the score tests cannot tell apart (the same class) are not refitted in the same round.

Where the shared dimensions are in blocks (popblocks in ctFit), the search acts on ctScoreTest's block tests. A block that needs a further dimension is given one, starting along the direction the test found (without blocks, the level's rank goes up by one). When the dimensions of two blocks covary, the blocks share them, and whichever block needs fewer new loadings to reach the other's effects is extended to them. A parameter that a change makes individually varying joins the block of the effects it should covary with (the initial means for a heterogeneity result, the intercept for a level result), unless a block already includes it. A block of full rank gains a dimension with it.

Each random effect the search adds brings correlations with the others, and with many random effects and few subjects the data no longer determine them. When a kept change leaves the population covariance poorly identified (fit$identifiability), the covariance is refitted at one rank lower (poprank), starting from its leading dimensions, and the lower rank is kept unless the likelihood ratio test needs the dropped dimension. This repeats until the fit is identified. Later random effects then load on the shared dimensions, and later heterogeneity results give own variances. This is for single level models only.

When the search stops, each change kept is tested again by refitting without it (prune), and dropped if the others make it unnecessary.

A relaxation is kept when its refit improves on the current model by criterion: a likelihood ratio test against a chi-square on the parameters the change adds, at alpha divided by the number of refits tried at that step ('LR'), or a lower AIC or BIC (with subjects as the sample size). The chi-square reference is only approximate for these changes. It is conservative for a new random effect, whose variance starts at zero, and can be wrong in either direction for a new process or cycle. Screening, rounds and pruning are further choices it does not count, so the p-values describe the steps the search took and do not test the final model. A refit that ends below the model it extends has not reached an optimum, and is recorded as such.

Error rates

Because the screen and the refit use the same data, the error rate is close to alpha for each decision, and grows with the number of families screened. In simulations with nothing missing, a one process model (80 subjects) kept a change in 5 per cent of searches at alpha = 0.05 and in none at alpha = 0.01, while a model of two processes with three items each, where state dependence and volatility are also screened in each process, kept a change in 4 of 20 searches at alpha = 0.05. For larger models alpha = 0.01 is the safer choice. criterion = 'BIC' was not stricter than 'LR' at these sizes. Small effects can be missed or replaced: a drift that varied over subjects was not found at 80 subjects, and a random diffusion or measurement error variance was sometimes added instead.

Selection and confirmation

The result is a model chosen by the data it is fitted to, and its standard errors and tests do not account for that choice (MacCallum, Roznowski & Necowitz, 1992). holdout sets aside a share of the subjects. The search runs on the rest, and each change it keeps is then tested on the held-out subjects alone, by refitting the final model without it there. confirmation says which changes held, and the final model, refitted to every subject, keeps only those. Every step, and every refit tried and rejected, is in history.

With many observations, the checks can reject a model for departures that are small. With close, the search also stops when every failing check is a residual or within row correlation family whose size is shown to be below close (see ctFitAdequacy).

Laplace fits

On a Laplace fit, a change that makes the dynamics depend on the state is refitted with the one-step Laplace approximation (optimcontrol$laplace_onestep in ctFit), and where the model has random dynamics, it is compared with the current model refitted the same way. To compare the models with their random effects integrated more exactly, start the search from a fit with intoverpop = 'quadrature', so that every refit is refined in the same way.
